text.title: Error Handling (RFC 7807 Problem Details) Decision Tree
text.summary: Protocol and commitment gate first, then preconditions and duplicate check. Routes to run / update / skip; every conclusion references a rule id from 01-core-rules.xml.

decision-tree.root-question: Are ALL preconditions satisfied? (prerequisite artefacts present AND named owner identifiable AND artefact store writable)

branch.question: Does an existing working artefact already cover this gap?

branch.conclusion: Skip: do not duplicate. Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
Run the procedure. Emit a new artefact per the output contract.
Skip this methodology. Surface the missing precondition. Defer until the gap is closed.
Not JSON over HTTP. gRPC uses `google.rpc.Status` + `error_details`; GraphQL puts errors in the response `errors[]` per spec; SSE/WebSocket frames follow their own conventions.
The framework cannot host one global handler. Do not ship per-route envelopes — solve the handler problem first, or the envelope drifts back apart within a sprint.
The team will not commit to stable `type` URIs or to `application/problem+json`. Skip: the envelope's value is the commitment, not the field list.

text.example:
inputs: {owner=alex@acme.com, prerequisites_present=true, existing_artefact=false} q-preconditions -> true q-duplicate -> false => conclusion run-the-checklist: emit new artefact.
second pass, implementation gate: protocol=rest-json-http, single_handler_supported=true, contract_commitment=true => run steps 6-10 of 04-procedure: URIs -> model -> one handler -> traceId -> contract test.
